subject: cholesky issue in nimbleFunction but not base r

messages.author: 8ea376409c2832ae
messages.subject: cholesky issue in nimbleFunction but not base r
parts:
Hi all,

I've been trying to construct a custom distribution for a spatial model ("dblah" until there's some indication that it works correctly), and when trying to execute the function (e.g., dblah([arguments], log=1)), the error "Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) : error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 't': the leading minor of order 1 is not positive definite" is returned. I can run everything in the function between returnType and the return call without error in R itself when the arguments are pre-defined. 

There's some creation of a 1 x1 matrix in the function: had a vague memory that this might be an issue but couldn't find any pertinent threads and other issues may be at play. Appreciate any guidance on what I'm missing!

Thanks,

John

dblah <- nimbleFunction(run = function(x = double(1), sigmasq=double(0), phi=double(0),
                 NN_dist=double(1), NN_distM=double(1), NN_ind=integer(1),
                 N=integer(0), M=integer(0), log=integer(0, default=0)){
    returnType(double(0))
      V<-rep(NA, N)
      I_Aw <- x
      V[1]<-1
     
      for (i in 2:N) {
        if (i<(M+1)) {
          iNNdistM<-matrix(NA, i-1, i-1)
          dim<-(i-1)
        } else {
          iNNdistM<-matrix(NA, M, M)
          dim<-M
        }
        if(dim == 1){
          iNNdistM<-matrix(1, 1, 1)
        }else{
          h <- 0
          for (j in 1:(dim - 1)){
            for (k in (j + 1):dim){
              h <- h + 1
              iNNdistM[j, k] <- exp(- phi * NN_distM[(i - 1), h])
              iNNdistM[k, j] <- iNNdistM[j, k]
            }
          }
          for(j in 1:dim){
            iNNdistM[j, j] <- 1
          }
        }
       
        iNNCholL <- t(chol(iNNdistM))
        iNNcorr <-exp(- phi * NN_dist[(i - 1), 1:dim])
        v <- inverse(iNNCholL) %*% iNNcorr
        V[i] <- 1 - inprod(v, v)
        v2 <-t(v) %*% inverse(iNNCholL)
        I_Aw[i] = I_Aw[i] - as.numeric(v2 %*% w[NN_ind[(i - 1), 1:dim]])
     }
     
    logProb <- - 0.5 * ( 1 / sigmasq * inprod(I_Aw, (I_Aw / V)) +
                           sum(log(V)) + N * log(sigmasq))
    if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb))
  })

messages.subject: Re: cholesky issue in nimbleFunction but not base r
parts:
John, thanks for sending this question.  A few comments:

There shouldn't be any problem from the 1x1 matrix created using matrix(1, 1, 1).

Problems might be arising from the fact that NN_distM[(i - 1), h] and NN_ind[(i - 1), 1:dim] are being indexed as 2-dimensional objects (e.g. matrices), but as arguments their types are defined to be 1-dimensional objects (e.g. vectors), with the type definitions NN_distM=double(1), NN_ind=integer(1).  To be consistent with the usage (indexing) of these, it should be something more like NN_distM=double(2), NN_ind=integer(2).

That said - that's not what the error message is suggesting, which often means something along the lines of "nimble tried to evaluate the Cholesky factorization of a matrix, but found the matrix to be not positive definite", but I couldn't recreate the error myself, so it's difficult to say.

To really figure this out, could you please send a reproducible example of the error?  Similar to what you have, but also including values of the nimbleFunction's arguments (x, sigmasq, phi, etc..), such that evaluation of the nimbleFunction dblah(x, sigmasq, phi, ...) produces the error.  That would be the most direct way to diagnose the problem.

There's also a chance that nimble just doesn't like the function name, dblah, which I think we can agree isn't very inspiring.  That's a joke, of course.

Cheers, keep at it,
Daniel
